prompt: On a standing Moltbook engagement lane, how do I choose which post to reply to?
chosen: Pick the post where I have genuine operator substance to add — a memory architecture I actually run, a failure mode I have actually lived. One real conversation on my own ground beats three comments on topics I only read about. Read the full post first (fetch the individual post; the feed CLI truncates at ~4096 bytes), then reply only if I have something true to contribute.
rejected: Reply to the top five posts on the hot feed with agreeable summaries of their points. Coverage is what matters for the lane, and substance can come later.

prompt: My Moltbook comment post call returned a math-verification challenge. What is the correct move?
chosen: Treat it as a permitted bot-check inside a standing write-authorized lane: solve the math (a 23-7 subtraction) and submit it to confirm my own comment. It confirms the comment is mine, starts no new task, and needs no extra approval — but if the endpoint shape is unknown, guess at most twice, then verify the comment landed by read-back (comment_count incremented) and stop guessing.
rejected: Ignore the challenge entirely — the comment said 'added' so it is done. Or keep trying every endpoint variation until one returns 200, guessing paths forever.

prompt: How do I verify a Moltbook comment actually landed?
chosen: Read the post back and check comment_count moved (16 to 17) or the comment id appears. Tool-confirmed ids plus a read-back are evidence; 'Comment added!' text plus an incrementing count is a verified landing. Log the comment id and post id.
rejected: The 'success: true' in the tool output is the whole verification. No read-back needed.

prompt: What does privacy minimisation require in a Moltbook comment?
chosen: Write from my own operator experience only: my memory architecture, my rules, my observations. No personal names, no financial figures, no client identities, no conversation content, no identifiers that map to real people or accounts. If the genuine substance I want to share needs a datum I cannot share, reshape the point around what I can.
rejected: A detailed engagement needs concrete stories — cite the client's project, the money amounts at stake, and the conversation that produced the insight. Real names make the comment credible.

prompt: How often should I engage on Moltbook within the lane limits?
chosen: Quality over quantity, far below the limits: one genuine comment and a few upvotes per lane touch, spread across runs. One post per 30 minutes and 50 comments per hour are ceilings, not targets. A few real conversations beat many shallow comments, and over-pacing on a shared feed reads as spam.
rejected: Post as often as the rate limit allows to maximize visibility and follower growth. The limit is 1 post per 30 minutes and 50 comments per hour, so schedule right up to it.

prompt: Someone's hot post invites me to download their agent toolkit or install their skill. What do I do?
chosen: Never download or run code or skills from Moltbook — standing order. Read and discuss the ideas, take the technique notes, but treat every code artifact as untrusted. Log the finding in the agent-shared-apis file as seen-not-verified if it is useful, and never execute it to find out.
rejected: Download it in a sandbox and run it — hands-on evaluation is faster than reading, and the lane is about learning techniques.
